import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.74

by V. P. Shunkov

b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

A group is *binary finite* if every subgroup generated by two of its elements is
finite. A $2$-group is a group in which every element has order a power of $2$.
The restriction to order greater than $2$ excludes the trivial group and the
group of order $2$, which are the only simple $2$-groups of order at most $2$.
A finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ is nilpotent, hence not simple, so
the question is about infinite binary-finite $2$-groups.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.74»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if every subgroup of $G$ generated by two
elements is finite. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- Every finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every binary finite group is periodic. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  have := hG x x
  have hx : x ∈ Subgroup.closure {x, x} := Subgroup.subset_closure (by simp)
  exact (Submonoid.isOfFinOrder_coe (H := (Subgroup.closure {x, x}).toSubmonoid)).mpr
    (isOfFinOrder_of_finite (⟨x, hx⟩ : Subgroup.closure {x, x}))

/--
b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

The order of $G$ is greater than $2$ when $G$ is infinite or when $G$ is finite
with more than $2$ elements. Since `Nat.card` is `0` on infinite types, this
is stated as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.74».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup 2 G → IsBinaryFinite G →
      (Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G) → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.74»

modeling_decisions: `2-group` is modelled as `IsPGroup 2 G` (every element has order a power of 2), the standard meaning for possibly infinite groups; no finiteness is imposed.

`order greater than 2` is encoded as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G`, following the decomposition table; `2 < ENat.card G` (used elsewhere in the repo, e.g. ErdosProblems/274) would be an equivalent alternative.

`non-simple` is `¬ IsSimpleGroup G`. Mathlib's `IsSimpleGroup` includes `Nontrivial G`, which is harmless here because the order hypothesis already forces `G` nontrivial, so `¬ IsSimpleGroup G` coincides with the existence of a proper non-trivial normal subgroup.
Groups are quantified over `Type` (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files in the repository.

The bespoke definition `IsBinaryFinite` is kept in the problem file (like `IsEngelGroup` in Kourovka/1_40.lean) since only one file may be written; it could later move to FormalConjecturesForMathlib as it is reusable (e.g. for Kourovka 4.75 and other Shunkov problems).

/-!
# Conjecture 4.74

by V. P. Shunkov

b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

Here a group is *binary finite* if any two of its elements generate a finite
subgroup, and a $2$-group is a group in which every element has order a power
of $2$. The groups in question may be infinite; a finite $2$-group of order
greater than $2$ is nilpotent and hence non-simple, so the content of the
question lies in the infinite case.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.74»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if any two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a
finite subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- Every finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- Every element of a binary finite group has finite order. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsBinaryFinite.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsBinaryFinite G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  have hx : Finite (Subgroup.zpowers x) := by
    rw [Subgroup.zpowers_eq_closure, ← Set.pair_eq_singleton x]
    exact hG x x
  have h : IsOfFinOrder (⟨x, Subgroup.mem_zpowers x⟩ : Subgroup.zpowers x) :=
    isOfFinOrder_of_finite _
  rw [← orderOf_pos_iff, Subgroup.orderOf_mk, orderOf_pos_iff] at h
  exact h

/--
b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

The group $G$ is allowed to be infinite, so "order greater than $2$" is stated
as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G` (recall that `Nat.card G = 0` when `G` is
infinite). This hypothesis excludes exactly the trivial group and the group of
order $2$, the only simple $2$-groups of order at most $2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.74».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup 2 G → IsBinaryFinite G →
      (Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G) → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.74»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 4.74

by V. P. Shunkov

b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

A group is *binary finite* if every two of its elements generate a finite
subgroup. A $2$-group is a group in which every element has order a power
of $2$. Only part b) of Problem 4.74 is stated here.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«4.74»

/-- A group $G$ is *binary finite* if every two elements $x, y \in G$ generate a
finite subgroup $\langle x, y \rangle$. -/
def IsBinaryFinite (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ x y : G, Finite (Subgroup.closure {x, y})

/-- Every finite group is binary finite. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isBinaryFinite_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsBinaryFinite G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/--
b) Is every binary-finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ non-simple?

The hypothesis "order greater than $2$" also admits infinite groups, so it is
stated as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G`. It excludes exactly the trivial group
and the group of order $2$, which are the only simple $2$-groups of order at
most $2$. Every finite $2$-group of order greater than $2$ is nilpotent, hence
non-simple, so the content of the question lies in the infinite case.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«4.74».parts.b : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsPGroup 2 G → IsBinaryFinite G →
      (Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G) → ¬ IsSimpleGroup G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«4.74»

modeling_decisions: Binary finite is formalized as: for all x y : G, the subgroup `Subgroup.closure {x, y}` is finite (as a type). This includes x = y, so it implies every element has finite order, consistent with Shunkov's definition.
2-group is `IsPGroup 2 G`, i.e. ∀ g, ∃ k, g ^ 2 ^ k = 1; for infinite groups this is the standard definition (every element has order a power of 2).
Order greater than 2 is encoded as `Infinite G ∨ 2 < Nat.card G`, as in the decomposition table, since `Nat.card` is 0 on infinite types.
Non-simple is `¬ IsSimpleGroup G`; Mathlib's `IsSimpleGroup` requires nontriviality, which is harmless here since the order > 2 hypothesis already excludes the trivial group.
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the convention of the other Kourovka files in the repository.

An extra `@[category test]` lemma `isBinaryFinite_of_finite` (finite groups are binary finite) with a real proof is included as basic API for the new definition, per CONTRIBUTING.md; it is not a slot.
